{"id": "d0661ed4-c23e-4e00-9681-6e7cdc404eb9", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Flow logs on my NAT gateway ENI show srcaddr 10.0.0.9 for all internet traffic. How do I find which instance is sending it?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "dfeca59f-c34d-47c3-8a81-3bab0bda951d", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is a how-to question about tracing a private IP back to its owning instance from NAT gateway flow logs, so I'm thinking through the practical steps someone would take to look this up—likely checking ENI descriptions, EC2 instance network interfaces, or VPC resource mappings for that IP.

{"id": "e64259a9-75a6-4e09-84f8-ff5cb2986945", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The private IP `10.0.0.9` is NAT'd on the way out, so NAT gateway flow logs will always show instance private IPs (not public/EIPs) as srcaddr — that's expected. To map it to an actual instance:

**1. Find the ENI/instance owning that private IP right now:**
```
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=addresses.private-ip-address,Values=10.0.0.9"
```
This works whether `10.0.0.9` is a primary or secondary private IP. The result includes the `attachment.instance-id`. (A narrower `describe-instances --filters "Name=private-ip-address,Values=10.0.0.9"` only catches primary IPs.)

**2. Watch out for IP reuse over time.** Private IPs get recycled when instances terminate and new ones launch into the same subnet. If the flow log entries span a wide time window, don't assume today's owner of `10.0.0.9` was always the owner — cross-check with CloudTrail `RunInstances`/`TerminateInstances` events or ENI attach/detach history for that time range to confirm who held the IP when the traffic was actually logged.

**3. If it's an ENI not attached to an instance** (e.g. ECS task, Lambda in VPC, or a load balancer), `describe-network-interfaces` will show `interface-type` and `requester-id`/`description` pointing to the owning service instead of an EC2 instance.

Want me to run the lookup now? If so, tell me the region (and account, if not the default agent space account) the NAT gateway and VPC are in, and I'll pull the ENI/instance details for `10.0.0.9`.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
